subtype: Approach: sharing the work with a sibling [Action]
passage: Akash and Jomon shared the balcony garden, and for a month they argued. "You never water!" "You never weed!" Then Akash hung a chart on the wall with two columns. Jomon: water each morning. Akash: weeds and dead leaves each evening. Each ticked their own box with a marker on a string. When exams began, the chart kept the plants alive even on nights when neither wanted to look up from the books, because each could see the other's ticks and did their part. Mummy said the tomatoes looked better than they had all holidays.

qa.q: Which job did Jomon take on the chart?
What were the brothers feeling before the chart, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Annoyed and resentful, since each said the other never did the work.

qa.q: What could the brothers do if one of them is ill, and why?
qa.a: They could swap jobs for a few days and note it on the chart, so the plants are still cared for and neither feels cheated.

qa.q: How might Mummy see the chart and the tomatoes?
qa.a: Mummy seems pleased, since the tomatoes looked better than during the holidays and the arguing had stopped.

grounding: Two brothers share garden jobs on a wall chart so neither feels the other does less and the plants survive exams.

subtype: Approach: sharing the work with a sibling [Action]
passage:
"Binod, I watered the chillies twice this week and you weeded nothing. Again."
"Because you were at cricket, Lakhan."
"So let's fix it. A chart." Lakhan taped a sheet to the wall by the back door. "Watering: you. Weeding: me. Tick when done."
"Why do I get watering? It's every day. Weeding is only twice a week."
"Fine. Then I also do the compost on Sundays."
"...Okay. That's fair."
Two weeks later, exams started.
"Binod, I have maths tomorrow. Can you do my weeding?"
"Only if you do my watering on Friday. That's my science day."
"Deal. Write it on the chart so Amma doesn't think I skipped."
Amma, passing, read the chart and laughed. "My two boys manage the plants better than I manage the kitchen."

qa.q: Where did Lakhan tape the chart?
qa.a: On the wall by the back door.

qa.q: Why did Binod object to watering at first?
qa.a: He felt resentful, since watering is every day and weeding only twice a week.

qa.q: What else could help the brothers during exams?
qa.a: They could ask Amma to cover one day a week in exam season, so neither has to trade jobs.

qa.q: How does Amma see the chart?
qa.a: Amma is amused and pleased, joking that her boys manage the plants better than she manages the kitchen.

grounding: Two brothers split watering and weeding on a wall chart so the work feels fair and the plants are cared for during exams.

subtype: Approach: sharing the work with a sibling [Action]
passage: Jomon and I are brothers, two years apart, and last year we nearly stopped speaking over a bed of tomatoes. I'm Nitin, the older one. I thought I did all the work; Jomon thought he did. So one Sunday we sat at the kitchen table with a big sheet of chart paper and made two columns. Watering, every evening: me. Weeding on Wednesday and Saturday, plus picking: Jomon. We stuck it on the wall and ticked it for three months. When my board exams came, Jomon took my watering for two weeks and wrote "exam swap" in the boxes. I did his weeding afterwards. The tomatoes never missed a day, and neither of us could say the other did less.

qa.q: What did Jomon write in the boxes during the exams?
How did Nitin feel about the work before the chart?
qa.a: Resentful, sure that he did all the work.

qa.q: What else could the brothers try to keep things fair?
qa.a: They could swap jobs every month, so each learns both tasks and neither feels stuck with the harder one.

qa.q: What was the chart like for Jomon?
qa.a: Jomon's work became visible, so he could not be accused of doing less, and he could help during Nitin's exams.

grounding: Looking back, a brother describes splitting garden jobs on a wall chart so neither felt the other did less, even in exam weeks.
